name: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome

reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / NCCN & genetics references
clinicalPearls: Most often caused by germline pathogenic variants in the BRCA1 or BRCA2 tumour suppressor genes, inherited autosomal dominantly, with other genes (e.g. PALB2) contributing to a broader hereditary breast cancer spectrum
Confers high lifetime risks of breast and ovarian (including fallopian tube and primary peritoneal) cancer, with earlier onset than sporadic disease
BRCA1-associated breast cancers are frequently triple-negative, while BRCA2 carriers have relatively higher rates of male breast cancer
BRCA2 also raises the risk of prostate and pancreatic cancer, and both genes are associated with an excess of contralateral and second primary breast cancers
Red-flag family features include multiple relatives with breast and/or ovarian cancer, young age at onset, bilateral disease, male breast cancer, and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry with founder variants
Enhanced surveillance for at-risk women centres on breast MRI in addition to mammography, starting at a younger age than population screening
Risk-reducing bilateral mastectomy and risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy substantially lower cancer incidence, with oophorectomy also reducing breast cancer risk in some carriers
Identification of a pathogenic variant informs treatment, as these tumours are sensitive to platinum agents and PARP inhibitors, and enables cascade testing of relatives
reference.pathophysiology: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumour suppressors essential for repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination. A germline loss-of-function variant in one allele, followed by somatic loss of the second, leaves cells reliant on error-prone repair pathways, producing genomic instability that drives carcinogenesis in hormonally responsive breast and ovarian epithelium. This same homologous recombination deficiency creates synthetic lethality that is exploited therapeutically by PARP inhibitors and confers sensitivity to platinum chemotherapy.
additionalDifferentials: Cowden syndrome and other PTEN hamartoma tumour syndromes
Sporadic or polygenic breast/ovarian cancer without a high-penetrance variant
additionalInvestigations: Germline BRCA1/BRCA2 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis, often within a multigene panel, with genetic counselling
Breast MRI combined with mammography for surveillance of at-risk women
Clinical breast examination and patient education on symptom awareness
Discussion of transvaginal ultrasound and CA-125 for ovarian risk, recognising their limited sensitivity, pending risk-reducing surgery
Consideration of prostate and pancreatic surveillance in relevant BRCA2 carriers
redFlags: Young-onset, bilateral, or triple-negative breast cancer
Ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer at any age
Male breast cancer or clustering of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancer in a family
New pelvic or abdominal symptoms in a carrier who has not undergone risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy
reference.prognosis: Lifetime breast and ovarian cancer risks are high but are substantially reduced by risk-reducing surgery and improved by intensive surveillance and early detection. Tumour prognosis depends on type and stage, and the availability of PARP inhibitors and platinum-based therapy has improved outcomes for many carriers.
pitfalls: Relying on mammography alone in high-risk women without adding breast MRI
Over-trusting ovarian screening, which is insufficiently sensitive, and delaying risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy
Testing only the affected patient and omitting cascade testing of at-risk relatives
Overlooking male carriers and their breast, prostate, and pancreatic cancer risks
management: Enhanced breast surveillance with annual breast MRI plus mammography beginning at a younger age than population screening
Discuss risk-reducing bilateral mastectomy as the most effective option for lowering breast cancer risk
Offer risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy after completion of childbearing to cut ovarian, fallopian tube and peritoneal cancer risk and mortality
Endocrine chemoprevention with selective oestrogen-receptor modulators or aromatase inhibitors in selected women
Treat BRCA-associated malignancy with platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors that exploit homologous-recombination deficiency
Consider prostate and pancreatic surveillance in relevant BRCA2 carriers, and support women through surgical menopause
Genetic counselling with germline BRCA1/BRCA2 testing and cascade screening of at-risk relatives
